_about: The author's multiple-choice answers for the Mode Build, word for word: every question the assistant asked from 2026-10-20 00:00 UTC (2026-10-19 17:00 Pacific) until this file was written (2026-10-21T06:22Z), with the options as offered and the label or labels the author picked. The assistant wrote the questions and the options, and marked some options as recommended; the picks are the author's. Times are UTC. Questions the author declined or did not answer are kept, marked as such. Taken from the Claude Code session record.
author: Aravind Sundaravadivelu

instruction_in_chat.text: signed in, build on the existing mode

questions.question: The picker chose a contractor role (Abacus Insights, "Contractor: DevOps Engineer"). Should the mode drop contract and temporary roles automatically?

options.label: Drop them (Recommended)
options.description: Contract and temporary roles rarely come with H-1B sponsorship, so for a candidate who needs sponsorship they waste a review slot.

options.label: Keep them
options.description: Let them through and judge each one by reading the posting at the human gate.

questions.question: The picker chose a PhD role (Databricks, "Systems PhD - Software Engineer"). Should the mode drop titles that require a PhD?

options.label: Drop them (Recommended)
options.description: The candidate is finishing a master's degree, so a PhD-only role is not open to them.

options.label: Keep them
options.description: Let them through and judge each one at the human gate.

questions.question: How many live postings should the mode send to the human gate for you to read?

options.label: 8, one per company (Recommended)
options.description: About 20–30 minutes of reading, and it covers eight different companies.

options.label: 5, one per company
options.description: Faster to review, but it covers fewer companies.

options.label: 10, one per company
options.description: Covers more companies, but takes longer to read.

questions.question: The sponsor tiers are my proposal: Proven = 10 or more approvals at 90%+ approved; Likely = 4 or more at 70%+. Keep them or change them?

options.label: Keep as proposed (Recommended)
options.description: Ten approvals means one filing or a double-counted record can't carry a company to the top tier, and 90% keeps out companies with a visible denial history.

options.label: Stricter: Proven needs 20+
options.description: Fewer companies reach the top tier, but each one has more evidence behind it.

options.label: Looser: Proven needs 6+
options.description: More companies reach the top tier, but more of them rest on only a few filings.

questions.question: Gate G0 (data age): the company table's newest funding date is 2025-09-26, about 13 months old, and the mode's limit is 6 months. Run anyway with a stale-data warning, or stop?

options.label: Run, with the warning (Recommended)
options.description: It's the only company data the repo has. The report says on its first screen that funding and sponsorship counts can be out of date, and the live posting check runs on today's job boards anyway.

options.label: Stop until the data is refreshed
options.description: No run until someone refreshes the upstream company table, which isn't possible before Wednesday.

questions.question: The discovery pool keeps companies that raised money within 24 months of the data's newest date. Keep 24 months?

options.label: Keep 24 months (Recommended)
options.description: Two years is a rough signal that a company may still be hiring. It isn't a tested predictor, and the report says so.

options.label: Tighten to 12 months
options.description: Only companies with a more recent raise, a smaller and fresher pool.

options.label: Widen to 36 months
options.description: A bigger pool, including companies whose last raise is older.

questions.question: The visa timeline gate assumes about 75 days from applying to a start date. Keep 75 days?

options.label: Keep 75 days (Recommended)
options.description: Roughly two and a half months for interviews, an offer, and onboarding. It's one assumption applied to every company, and the report labels it as yours.

options.label: Use 60 days
options.description: Assume a faster hiring process.

options.label: Use 90 days
options.description: Assume a slower process, which leaves more buffer.

options.description: The cap of 8 chose among equal scores by alphabet: Zscaler (802 approvals) was left out while Xage (24) was kept

questions.question: Databricks's posting says that if a job needs export-controlled technology, they may decline an applicant who would need a government license. You marked it "Looks fine". What should the mode's rule be for a clause like that?

options.label: Pass, show the quote
options.description: It's a condition, not a no. The posting can clear, and the report keeps the quoted sentence so the reader sees it. Databricks stays cleared (7 cleared).

options.label: Hold, ask a recruiter
options.description: The posting waits until a recruiter confirms the role doesn't need export-controlled work. Databricks moves to held (6 cleared, 1 held).

options.label: Block it
options.description: Any export-control clause sets the posting aside. Databricks moves to set aside (6 cleared, 2 set aside).
